SYNTHETIC LAB & DESIGN
Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

Operate stores; govern entities.

Infrastructure management and customer federation remain distinct control planes.

Proposed pilot design

This page describes a target design. The local lab and browser models demonstrate bounded subsets; the proposal is not production acceptance. Understand the labels.

Start with the example · Look up a term

Two inventories

InventoryContainsAuthority
Store fleetCluster ID, site, country, racks/AZs, keys, backups and network endpointsInfrastructure operations.
Entity directoryLegal entity ID, business group, approved storage countries, primary store binding/versionEntity governance plus data-policy authority.
Customer relationshipsOwner, global ID, sharing grants, exclusions and field profilesAuthoritative owner application and policy service.

PoC versus production

The base data examples use three geographic stores. The unified lab provisions a fourth store for India migration, four OPA services, a FastAPI monitor/worker, an HTTP gateway and an OTel Collector. Only the local UI/API port is exposed to the host. It models placement, not actual countries. Production requires independent site deployment, approved credentials, TLS, operator support and local quorum resilience.

Recovery must preserve policy

01Identify approved target

Entity and every affected customer permit the physical country.

02Fence the old writer

No two authoritative owner copies may accept mutations.

03Restore in quarantine

Apply current policy and generation state before serving.

04Prove and admit

Check placement, data freshness and access; record evidence.

A region outage does not authorise a geography exception

An entity with no permitted recovery location becomes unavailable. Do not silently rebind it to the nearest healthy store. Infrastructure control-plane availability must not be a hidden dependency of every customer write.

Entity relocation decision: keep legal entity identity stable while changing physical home. Use a lawful transition policy, snapshot plus continuous change capture, versioned tombstones, target-applied checkpoints, graph closure and an entity-specific source writer fence. Persist source fencing before activating the target; never flip routing back after target writes. Separate placement version, writer epoch, policy revision and resource data version. Migration consumes the capped bulk lane; guard and operational capacity remain reserved. The executable edition-08 slice uses isolated mig_* row envelopes and one coordinator; it does not migrate the original normalized business.* fixture or prove distributed fencing. Read Entity relocation before implementation.

Design production infrastructure overlays independently from entity policies. Pin operator/database versions and validate platform support. Add a separate HA profile with real local failure-domain tests. Keep one-node Compose as the baseline synthetic demo. Never infer that an entity/store directory replaces physical replica and backup verification.
